briefdescription.para: Signs a test message using the generated SLH-DSA secret key.

inbodydescription.para: Sign the test message as pure SLH-DSA with an empty context and hedged add_rand. This is the FIPS 205 default path and is run for every parameter set.

briefdescription.para: Runs keygen, sign, and verify for one SLH-DSA parameter set.

inbodydescription.para: Validate input pointer.
Step 1: generate a key pair into the shared buffers consumed by the sign and verify stages below, so this stage must run first.
Invalidate the key buffers, which ASUFW wrote by DMA, over the per-variant sizes rather than the maximum buffer sizes.
Step 2: sign the test message with the secret key just generated.
Invalidate the signature buffer before it is passed back for verification.
Step 3: verify the signature with the matching public key.
SHAKE-128s is the cheapest extra sign, so the remaining FIPS modes (non-empty context, HashSLH-DSA and deterministic signing) are exercised on this key pair only when extra-mode coverage is enabled.
SHA2-256s requires SHA-512 as PH(M) (FIPS 205 footnote 18, n = 32), so HashSLH-DSA SHA-512 is exercised on this key pair only when that coverage is enabled.

briefdescription.para: Runs the extra FIPS 205 modes on one SHAKE-128s key pair.

inbodydescription.para: Validate input pointer.
Stage 1: pure SLH-DSA with a non-empty context. Sign and verify must use the same CtxAddr and CtxLen, because the context is bound into the message digest.
Stage 2: HashSLH-DSA. PH(M) is SHA-256 of the test message and is computed on the client; ASUFW hashes 0x01 || ctx_len || ctx || OID || PH(M).
Stage 3: deterministic signing. add_rand is derived from PK.seed rather than the TRNG, with the default empty context so this path is distinct from stage 1.

briefdescription.para: Runs HashSLH-DSA with SHA-512 PH(M) on one SHA2-256s key pair.

inbodydescription.para: Validate input pointer.

PH(M) is SHA-512 of the test message. HashId must be SHA-512 for 256s sets so that PH(M) is at least 2n bytes. The empty context keeps this path distinct from the SHAKE-128s HashSLH-DSA sequence, which already used a non-empty context.

briefdescription.para: Computes SHA-256 or SHA-512 PH(M) of the test message for HashSLH-DSA.

inbodydescription.para: Reset the callback status so the wait observes this SHA2 request only.
Hash the test message; the digest is the HashSLH-DSA PH(M).

Send the sign request to ASUFW.
Queue AES immediately so the server can pick it on the next yield slice. AES uses a second unique ID and callback.

detaileddescription.para: This example demonstrates SLH-DSA key generation, message signing, and signature verification using the xilasu client APIs over IPI to ASUFW. The flow is exercised for all four supported FIPS 205 parameter sets: SHAKE-256s, SHAKE-128s, SHA2-256s, and SHA2-128s.

For each parameter set the example:
Generates an SLH-DSA key pair.
Signs a test message with the generated secret key.
Verifies the signature with the generated public key.

SHAKE-128s can also run three extra sign/verify sequences on the same key pair: a non-empty FIPS context, HashSLH-DSA (SHA-256 PH(M)), and deterministic signing. SHA2-256s can additionally run HashSLH-DSA with SHA-512 PH(M). SHAKE-256s can queue an AES-GCM encrypt immediately after the default sign so that ASUFW can pick AES on a yield slice. Both requests must succeed; their completion order is printed and is not a pass/fail check. SHAKE-128s can also run an ACVP known-answer test whose pure message exceeds the SHA DMA blocking size: verify the published signature, then sign deterministically and compare. Those extra paths are off by default; set the matching XASU_SLHDSA_EXAMPLE_*_ENABLE macros to 1U to turn them on.
Client buffers passed to ASUFW must reside in memory visible to both client and server. See the linker-script notes in xasu_sha2_example.c for OCM/shared-memory placement.

IPI command flow demonstrated:
XAsu_ClientInit initializes the mailbox and client layer.
For each parameter set, XAsu_KmGenerateSlhdsaKeyPair sends keygen parameters (SkOutAddr, SkOutLen, PkOutAddr, PkOutLen, ParamSet) to the key manager and waits for the IPI callback.
XAsu_SlhdsaSign sends sign parameters (message, secret key, signature output, context. When AES overlap is enabled, SHAKE-256s immediately queues an AES-GCM encrypt so ASUFW can pick AES during a sign yield slice. The example prints the completion order of the two requests.
XAsu_SlhdsaSignVerify sends verify parameters with matching CtxLen and ParamSet.
When extra modes are enabled, SHAKE-128s runs three further sign/verify sequences on the same key pair: non-empty context, HashSLH-DSA SHA-256, and deterministic signing.
When SHA-512 pre-hash is enabled, SHA2-256s signs and verifies HashSLH-DSA with SHA-512 PH(M).
When the large-message KAT is enabled, SHAKE-128s verifies and signs the ACVP vector in xasu_slhdsa_example_largemsg.h (5377-byte pure message).

DMA buffer requirements:
Secret key, public key, message, and signature buffers are placed in dedicated linker sections (.data.XAsu_Slhdsa*) for shared-memory visibility.
Buffer sizes use XASU_SLHDSA_MAX_* constants; per-variant sizes come from XAsu_SlhdsaGetSkSize, XAsu_SlhdsaGetPkSize, and XAsu_SlhdsaGetSigSize.
